stories.headline: Researcher finds zero-day that hands attackers control of Meta's Muse
stories.standfirst: Patrick Wardle said any local app can steal the token that controls a Muse account. Meta did not answer questions from Ars Technica.
body: Any app or terminal command running on a Mac can seize control of a user's Muse account, the security researcher Patrick Wardle told Ars Technica. Meta released the assistant a few weeks ago. Wardle said he has written several working proof-of-concept attacks against it.

The flaw sits in a list of undocumented settings that Meta lets any local process change, according to Wardle. Most control cosmetic things such as dark mode. One sets the server address where Muse sends speech for transcription, and pointing it at an attacker's machine hands over the account token.

"We can manipulate the agent and leverage its privileges to do whatever we want," Wardle said. He said the attacks can write files to disk and take photographs with no sign to an alert user. A variant of the ClickFix technique is enough to start one.

Meta has published two posts in as many weeks on the design decisions behind Muse, and Mark Zuckerberg has said the assistant is built from the ground up for privacy and security. Meta representatives did not answer emailed questions, Ars Technica said.

Wardle said Muse could have avoided the flaw by transcribing speech on the device, as macOS allows, rather than in Meta's cloud. The account rests on Wardle's own testing, and Meta has not said whether it plans a fix. He may give more detail at a conference in November.

stories.headline: UK AI Safety Institute staff take stress leave, Financial Times says
stories.standfirst: Four people told the newspaper that testing schedules for unreleased models and alarm at their capabilities have left morale low and several staff on leave.
body: Multiple staff at the UK's AI Safety Institute are off work with stress and undergoing counselling, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday. The paper attributed the account to people with knowledge of the matter, and gave no number.

Four people told the FT that tight schedules for testing unreleased models, and alarm at how quickly those models are gaining capability, had contributed to low morale and burnout. The account rests on the FT's reporting alone.

A former researcher at the institute said the cyber and bio teams were the most alarmed by recent jumps in capability. The models can now find undiscovered flaws in code and produce viruses “unknown in nature”, the former researcher said.

A DeepMind employee described “various quittings and a lot of mental health leave”, and said the pace of the work is not compatible with safety. The FT did not name the employee and gave no figure for departures.

The FT describes the institute as the global leader in independent testing of frontier models. That characterisation is the paper's, not a claim from the institute. What the reported strain means for the testing schedule is not addressed in the account.

stories.headline: CFTC to open Frontier Forum roundtables with session on agentic finance
stories.standfirst: The derivatives regulator's Innovation Task Force will hold its first public roundtable on artificial intelligence and agentic finance on 28 October, the agency said.
body: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission said on Monday that its Innovation Task Force will host a series of public roundtables called the Frontier Forum. The first session, on artificial intelligence and agentic finance, is set for 28 October.

The commission described the series as a venue for builders and leaders from the public and private sectors to discuss responsible innovation while protecting market integrity. That description is the agency's. No agenda, speaker list or registration process has been published.

Chairman Michael Selig said in the statement that the technologies transforming American markets are advancing fast. He said the agency must engage directly with the people who build and use them. The commission gave no further detail on who will attend.

The public may nominate speakers by email, the commission said, though it added that in-person places may be limited by security requirements. Details on the agenda, the speakers and registration are to be announced later.

stories.headline: Finnish AI cloud Verda raises $189 million led by Emergence Capital
stories.standfirst: The Helsinki company said the round values it at more than $1 billion and brings total funding above $450 million across equity and debt.
body: Verda, a Finnish cloud company that rents out GPU capacity, has raised $189 million in a round led by Emergence Capital, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday. The company said the financing values it at $1 billion or more, and declined to give an exact figure.

MUFG Innovation Partners, Super Micro Computer, Varma Mutual Pension Insurance and Lifeline Ventures also took part, according to Bloomberg. Verda said the round was oversubscribed and brings its total funding past $450 million across equity and debt. Those figures are the company's own.

The company started in 2020 as DataCrunch and took the Verda name late in 2025. It said it is cash-flow positive on a revenue run rate above $60 million. Bloomberg attributed both of those figures to Verda rather than to a filing.

Verda positions itself as a European alternative to Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure, and says it runs its own data centres and networking. That positioning is the company's, and Bloomberg did not report independent figures on its capacity or its customers.

stories.headline: Morphotonics raises €40 million to take imprint tooling into data centres
stories.standfirst: The Dutch nanoimprint lithography company said the money will fund a move from augmented-reality waveguides into co-packaged optics for data centre servers.
body: Morphotonics, a Dutch maker of nanoimprint lithography equipment, has raised €40 million from investors including 3M Ventures, the European Innovation Council Fund and the European Investment Bank, TechCrunch reported on Monday. The report named no lead investor.

Innovation Industries, BOM, Invest-NL and the Dutch family office Ernij Next also took part, according to TechCrunch. The round extends a raise the company began in 2024 and has been paid in installments, the report said, so the €40 million is not new money arriving at once.

Nanoimprint lithography presses a stamp into photosensitive material. Morphotonics has used it to make waveguides, the thin sheets that bend light across the lens of a pair of smart glasses. The company now wants to make co-packaged optics, which move data between servers inside a data centre.

Customers have validated the data centre technology, according to TechCrunch, but no machines have shipped. The company said its next machine will produce more than 6 million waveguides a year and ships in early 2027. That output figure is a company claim.

Morphotonics has about 60 staff, up from roughly 30 in September 2024, and is aiming for 70 to 75. Chief executive Hugo Da Silva said a strong local presence matters to customers, with most display manufacturing concentrated in China, Taiwan, South Korea and the United States.

stories.headline: MIT Technology Review maps deaths near AI border surveillance towers
stories.standfirst: A 15-month investigation with Times of San Diego found people who walked undetected past AI-enabled towers and died nearby, the outlet said.
body: MIT Technology Review published an investigation on Monday into deaths near the surveillance towers the US government has installed along its border with Mexico. Journalists at both newsrooms spent 15 months on the work, which the outlets call Dying on Camera.

The investigation describes what it calls the first comprehensive map of deaths along the line of towers. Reporters found cases of people who walked undetected through areas the AI-enabled towers were meant to watch, and who later died nearby, where their bodies went unnoticed. The mapping and the count are the outlets' own, and no other newsroom has published a comparable figure.

One case is José Morales Bernal, who crossed into the United States on 8 April 2024, the day before his 32nd birthday. He walked through the desert in southern New Mexico within range of three towers, according to the investigation.

A second account follows Graciela Gómez Hernández, 30, who crossed from the eastern edge of Tijuana into Southern California on 14 September 2025. She sent voice messages to her mother and sister as she walked, and a surveillance camera stood in plain sight, the reporters wrote.

The outlets published a companion piece setting out four changes they say could address the failures. The US government has spent billions of dollars on border surveillance, the investigation said. The published summaries do not carry a response from the agencies that operate the towers.

stories.headline: TSMC to start A14 trial production in early 2027, newspaper says
stories.standfirst: Commercial Times, citing chip-design houses, said the A14 CyberShuttle ran in the second quarter of 2026, while TSMC's two prior nodes are still ramping.
body: Trial production of TSMC's A14 process is due in the first quarter of 2027 at Fab 20 in Hsinchu Baoshan, the Taiwanese newspaper Commercial Times reported, citing chip-design houses. The account SemiconductorsX relayed the report on X on Tuesday.

The volume site is Taichung Fab 25, according to the report. The report puts completion there before the second quarter of 2027, with trial runs to follow. TSMC has not published a schedule for A14, and the newspaper attributes the dates to design houses rather than to the company.

The A14 CyberShuttle already ran in the second quarter of 2026, the report said. That puts the shuttle run three quarters ahead of the trial production date. The report does not say which customers may have taken part.

The story rests on one Taiwanese newspaper, relayed by one account on X, and no second outlet has carried the same dates. The report as relayed carries no comment from TSMC, and the company has not confirmed the fab assignments.

stories.headline: Amazon Bedrock adds xAI's Grok 4.6 with 500K token context window
stories.standfirst: AWS said the model runs on two Bedrock endpoints, with four reasoning effort levels and support for cross-Region inference.
body: xAI's Grok 4.6 is now available in Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Web Services said in a post on Monday. The company put the context window at 500,000 tokens and described the model as built for long-running agents and for coding.

The characterisation is xAI's and Amazon's own, offered in a vendor post. AWS published no benchmark scores with the announcement, and no independent evaluation of Grok 4.6 running on Bedrock has appeared in the material available so far.

The model runs on both the bedrock-mantle and bedrock-runtime endpoints, AWS said, with Converse API and cross-Region inference support. The post lists four reasoning effort levels, and does not say what separates them. AWS gave no price for the model in the post.

Grok 4.6 is the version before Grok 4.7. The account theo, posting on X, said Grok 4.7 does not beat Grok 4.6 on many benchmarks, and called Grok 4.6 slower and more expensive than Grok 4.5. Those are one user's assessments, and may not hold across other tasks.

stories.headline: Tencent launches Hy Image 3.5 Preview, says it matches Seedream 5.0 Pro
stories.standfirst: The comparison with ByteDance's image model comes from Tencent's internal testing, according to a Bloomberg report relayed on Tuesday.
body: Tencent has launched Hy Image 3.5 Preview, an image model, according to a Bloomberg report that the aggregator Techmeme relayed on Tuesday. Tencent said that in internal testing the model reached results on par with ByteDance's Seedream 5.0 Pro.

The comparison is Tencent's own, drawn from tests the company ran and selected. No independent benchmark of Hy Image 3.5 Preview against Seedream 5.0 Pro has been published, and ByteDance has not responded to the claim in the material available.

The relayed report does not give a release date, a price, or the regions where the model is available. It does not say whether Tencent has released weights, or whether the preview is open to developers outside China.

The story rests on one outlet. Bloomberg has it, and no second newsroom has carried the launch in the material gathered so far. The preview label suggests the model may still change before a wider release.

stories.headline: Belgian AI recruitment startup Spott raises $21 million Series A
stories.standfirst: Balderton led the round, with Base10, Y Combinator and Fortino taking part, bringing the company's total funding to $24 million.
body: Spott, a recruitment platform based in Belgium, has raised $21 million in a Series A led by Balderton, according to a report by Chris Metinko for Axios that Techmeme relayed on Tuesday. Base10, Y Combinator and Fortino also took part.

The round brings Spott's total funding to $24 million, the report said. The report describes Spott as an AI recruitment platform. Neither the valuation nor the use of proceeds appears in the relayed report, and it carries no comment from Balderton.

The story rests on one outlet. Axios has it, and no second newsroom has carried the round in the material gathered so far. The $24 million total implies about $3 million raised before this round, though the report does not break that figure down.

stories.headline: Alibaba plans model of 5 to 10 trillion parameters, launches AI chip
stories.standfirst: Chief executive Eddie Wu set out the plan at Alibaba Cloud's Apsara Conference in Hangzhou, alongside a new accelerator and a 20 gigawatt data centre target.
body: Alibaba plans to train a model with between 5 trillion and 10 trillion parameters, chief executive Eddie Wu said Tuesday at the company's Apsara Conference in Hangzhou. Reuters reported the remarks. Wu gave no timetable for the training run and did not say what hardware would carry it.

Alibaba's chip unit T-Head announced an accelerator called the Zhenwu V900 at the same event. Bloomberg reported that Alibaba puts its performance at three times that of the previous part, and says a single cluster can scale to 500,000 of them. Both figures are the company's own.

Wu also said Alibaba Cloud aims to hold more than 20 gigawatts of data centre capacity worldwide by 2032, according to a market wire carrying his remarks. Bloomberg reported the same target. Alibaba describes the Zhenwu V900 as the most powerful AI chip in China.

No independent testing of the chip supports that description. Alibaba has not published a specification sheet for the Zhenwu V900, and the three-times figure is measured against a part the company also makes. Fast market wires carried the chip's designation inconsistently on Tuesday, with one reporting it as the V300.

The parameter range is a statement of intent rather than a shipped model. Wu did not say whether the count refers to total parameters or to the smaller number active on each token, a distinction that changes what the figure means. Alibaba has not said when training would begin.

stories.headline: British Columbia sues OpenAI, says warning could have averted shooting
stories.standfirst: The province filed in California on Monday, arguing the company should have told police what it knew about a user before a mass shooting at a school.
body: British Columbia has sued OpenAI in California over a mass shooting at a school in the province, Reuters reported. The province filed on Monday and says the shooting could have been prevented if the company had warned local law enforcement about the user beforehand.

The claim turns on a duty to warn. Reuters reported that the province contends OpenAI held information about the user that it did not pass to police. That is an allegation in a complaint, not a finding, and no court has tested it.

Canadian and international outlets carried the filing on Monday and Tuesday, placing the shooting at a secondary school in Tumbler Ridge, in northern British Columbia, in February. Reports of the complaint say the province seeks compensation and an order changing how the company handles conversations that threaten violence.

OpenAI's answer to the suit is not yet reported. The paper has not seen the complaint, and the account of what the company knew rests on the province's own characterisation of its evidence. What OpenAI recorded about the user, and when, is not established.

stories.headline: Artificial Analysis puts Gemini 3.1 Flash top of new speech benchmark
stories.standfirst: The evaluator's new pronunciation test measures how often text-to-speech models read difficult text correctly, and puts Google's entry at 88.1 percent.
body: Artificial Analysis said on Tuesday it has begun scoring text-to-speech models on what it calls "pronunciation robustness", a measure of how often a model reads challenging text correctly. The evaluator put Google's Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS top at 88.1 percent, at a listed $18.31 per million characters.

SpaceXAI TTS scored 87.6 percent at $15 per million characters, which Artificial Analysis called the lowest price of any model above 80 percent. Kokoro 82M v1.0 is the cheapest the evaluator listed, at $0.65 per million characters. Those are list prices, according to the evaluator, and not measured cost.

Speed and accuracy do not track each other in the results. Kokoro 82M v1.0 is the fastest model Artificial Analysis posted, at 242 characters a second. Realtime TTS-2 Flash reached 220 characters a second and scored 77.8 percent. SpaceXAI TTS ran at 106 characters a second.

The scores diverge from listener preference. Sonic 3.6 holds the highest Provider Voice Arena Elo of the group at 1276 while scoring 74.5 percent on the new test, the evaluator said. Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS sits at 1201 Elo. Both rankings are its own.

The test breaks into sub-scores. Artificial Analysis said Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS leads on contextually appropriate pronunciation at 96.4 percent and on expanding shorthand at 84.4 percent, against 84.3 percent for SpaceXAI TTS. SpaceXAI TTS leads on preserving exact sequences at 85.7 percent.

stories.headline: Artificial Analysis scores StepFun's Step 5 Preview at 44 on its index
stories.standfirst: The evaluator said the model matches Kimi K3 at about a third of the cost per task, but trails rivals on agentic work.
body: StepFun's Step 5 Preview scores 44 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, level with Kimi K3 at its maximum setting, the evaluator said on Monday. The model has 600 billion total parameters and 27 billion active, and succeeds Step 3.7 Flash, released in May 2026.

Artificial Analysis put the cost of running its index on Step 5 Preview at about $0.72 per task. It said Kimi K3 at maximum cost about $2.00 for the same score, and GLM-5.3 at maximum about $2.01 for one point more. The evaluator's page lists the model at $1 per million input tokens and $2.70 per million output tokens.

The gap is on agentic work. Artificial Analysis said Step 5 Preview sits behind GLM-5.3 at maximum and Qwen3.8 Max on GDPval-AA, at 1,566 Elo against 1,646 and 1,668, and on AA-Briefcase, at 1,432 against 1,525 and 1,640. On Terminal-Bench 4.0 it scored 33% against 42% and 39%.

On knowledge the ordering reverses. The evaluator reported 46% on Humanity's Last Exam against 42% and 43% for the same two models, and 42% on AA-Omniscience against 34% for GLM-5.3 at maximum and 48% for Kimi K3 at maximum. Step 5 Preview has 600 billion total parameters against 753 billion and 2.8 trillion.

Token use does not explain the price gap, Artificial Analysis said, putting Step 5 Preview at about 164 million output tokens to run the index against about 170 million for Kimi K3 at maximum. It said the model hallucinates on 43% of attempts rather than declining to answer. The index combines several evaluations, according to Artificial Analysis, and every figure here comes from that one group.

stories.headline: Microsoft doubles Taiwan AI data centre plan to 4 sites, manager says
stories.standfirst: Bian Zhixiang also said Microsoft's own AI chips should reach mass production in 2027, in remarks reported by Economic Daily News.
body: Microsoft will expand its AI data centres in Taiwan from two sites to four, the general manager of Taiwan Microsoft, Bian Zhixiang, said in remarks reported on Tuesday by Economic Daily News. The account dnystedt, relaying the report on X, said the two new sites will be in Gueishan and Luzhu in northern Taiwan.

Bian put the shortage of computing capacity at two to three years, and said semiconductor and high-technology companies are Microsoft's largest customers in Taiwan. He said the company cannot spare capacity for third parties, and is prioritising its own AI services to raise supply and cut running costs.

On Microsoft's in-house chips, Bian said design and capacity were proceeding smoothly, with mass production expected in 2027. The assessment is Microsoft's own, offered by its Taiwan manager. Microsoft has not published a production schedule for the parts.

Outside reports cited by the newspaper put the Maia 300 chip as arriving later this year, with talks under way with TSMC for capacity above 300,000 units and delivery targeted for 2027. The report does not attribute those figures to either company. The story rests on one newspaper, and no second outlet has carried the same detail.

stories.headline: LG, Microsoft agree to explore data centre cooling deal, newspaper says
stories.standfirst: Chairman Koo Kwang-mo met Satya Nadella in Redmond, and the two companies will look at LG supplying power and cooling gear, the Seoul Economic Daily reported.
body: LG and Microsoft have agreed to explore having LG supply large-scale cooling and power equipment for Microsoft's expanding AI data centres, the Seoul Economic Daily reported on Tuesday. IT infrastructure is also in scope. LG's chairman, Koo Kwang-mo, met Microsoft's chief executive, Satya Nadella, in Redmond, Washington.

The near-term focus is cooling for selected Microsoft sites, the newspaper said. Prefabricated data centres, built from pre-manufactured components, are a medium- to long-term aim. LG would combine LG Electronics' heating and air-conditioning technology with LG CNS's work building and running data centres.

The agreement extends to what the two companies call physical AI, covering manufacturing and logistics as well as mobility. The newspaper described the aim as a data flywheel. Factory-floor data would train models on Microsoft's cloud, and the models would then improve performance at production sites.

LG will also adopt Microsoft's Copilot and other AI tools for office staff worldwide, according to the report. It said no financial figures or production targets were disclosed. The account PhotonCap, which circulated the report on X, gave the same outline and added no terms.

stories.headline: OpenAI is preparing always-on agent called Aeon, two accounts say
stories.standfirst: Neither account cites a document or an OpenAI statement, and the company has not confirmed that the agent exists.
body: OpenAI is preparing an always-on agent named Aeon, two accounts that follow the company closely said on Monday. Kol Tregaskes described it as ChatGPT's answer to Grok Bot. Neither account cited a document or an OpenAI statement, and OpenAI has not said that the product exists.

Andrew Curran said the name is Aeon, that OpenAI built it ahead of schedule with help from GPT-Astra, and that he believes it will arrive on Thursday morning. Curran offered the timing as his own belief rather than as something a source had told him.

The two posts sit against agents already shipping. Meta released Muse this month, and SpaceXAI runs Grok Bot, the product Tregaskes named as OpenAI's target. The account MTSlive said on Monday that personal agents are reaching a mainstream audience across all three.

Nothing in either post can be checked against an OpenAI source. The company has not announced an agent by that name, and a date resting on one observer's belief may move. OpenAI has referred to GPT-6 Astra in its own posts, in a note about a customer's video tools.

stories.headline: Apple opens claims in $250 million settlement over AI Siri delay
stories.standfirst: US owners of the iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 16 have until 21 December to file, with an estimated $25 per device.
body: Apple is taking claims in a $250 million settlement over its failure to ship an AI-upgraded Siri alongside the iPhone 16, The Verge reported on Monday. US buyers of the iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max or any iPhone 16 model qualify.

The purchase must fall between 10 June 2024 and 29 March 2025, and claims close on 21 December 2026, according to The Verge. Payouts are estimated at $25 per eligible device. The settlement website says that figure could rise to $95 depending on how many people file.

The class action alleged Apple created a clear and reasonable consumer expectation that AI features previewed at WWDC 2024 would arrive with the iPhone 16. The phone shipped with a narrower set of capabilities while carrying the label built for Apple Intelligence, the complaint said.

Apple has denied any wrongdoing. The company later delayed the AI-upgraded Siri, which arrived with iOS 27 earlier this month, according to The Verge. MacRumors reported the opening of claims first, The Verge said. Filing requires a name, contact details and an iPhone serial number.
